title: Your workspace
desc: Start an agent, find your bearings, and follow the work.

chapters.title: Start a session
chapters.heading: Fix the checkout timeout
steps: Open Agents and create a session. Choose your provider, model, and repository.
Give the agent a concrete task. Its terminal stays live while it works.
Split or tile sessions to compare work. Reopen a session when you need to continue.

chapters.title: Follow the work
chapters.heading: Checkout reliability
steps: Open Mission Control to see related work in one place.
Select a work item to inspect its status, links, and evidence.
Follow the linked session or review when you need to act.

chapters.title: Make room to think
chapters.heading: Your workspace, arranged for you
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance, to choose your theme and arrange the sidebar.
Keep the pages you use most within reach. Hide entries you rarely need.
Press Command K to find a command and move straight to the next task.

title: From change to proof
desc: Inspect a change, review it, and follow the evidence to approval.

chapters.title: Inspect the change
chapters.heading: Retry only transient failures
steps: Open Git and choose your repository. Inspect the working changes before staging.
Select a file to read its diff. Stage only the changes you intend to commit.
Use the branch graph and pull requests to keep the change in context.

chapters.title: Bring different lenses
chapters.heading: Review the retry change
steps: Open Review for a pull request or your working tree. Choose review lenses and providers.
Open a reviewer session to inspect its work. Triage the collected findings.
Hand a finding to an agent, then verify the fix before resolving it.

chapters.title: Read the evidence
chapters.heading: What supports completion?
steps: Open the linked Proof Pack. Inspect test output, snapshots, and attached artifacts.
Check the derived status. Missing evidence or a failed check still needs attention.
Use the evidence to decide whether the work is ready for approval.

chapters.title: Start from the task
chapters.heading: Turn a source item into a PR draft
steps: Open Run with Otto. Choose a source item, repository, provider, and model.
Follow the run through implementation, evidence, and review. Inspect anything that needs attention.
At the approval gate, review the result before allowing the pull request draft.

title: From idea to context
desc: Refine a story, explore the web, and preserve what the team learns.

chapters.title: Refine the story
chapters.heading: Retry checkout safely
steps: Import a Jira issue or Confluence page into Product. Open its analysis.
Resolve the questions, inspect the rewrite, and refine the test cases and plan.
Create a mockup when a screen helps. Inject the refined context into an agent.

chapters.title: Make the idea visible
chapters.heading: A shared view of checkout
steps: Open Canvas and create a scene. Choose Excalidraw, Mermaid, or D2.
Describe the flow to the agent. Watch the scene update as the source changes.
Refine the diagram in the conversation until it explains the idea clearly.

chapters.title: Research with context
chapters.heading: Understand the retry contract
items: Save the source with your notes
steps: Open Browser and navigate to a reference. Choose Reader, or Live in the desktop app.
Mark the passages or elements that matter. Add a note about what to investigate.
Send the marks into a session, or save the page and notes to Vault.

chapters.title: Keep the knowledge
chapters.heading: Checkout reliability notes
steps: Open Vault and select a vault folder. Create or open a note.
Link related notes and use search to find the knowledge you need.
Keep decisions, references, and runbooks connected to the work they explain.

title: Work that keeps moving
desc: Choose the right kind of automation, with clear limits and visible progress.

chapters.title: Build an agent team
chapters.heading: Checkout reliability team
steps: Open Swarm and create a team. Give each role a clear responsibility.
Start the project and follow assignments on the board and run view.
Open an agent session when work needs direction. Review the team result.

chapters.title: Give iteration a boundary
chapters.heading: Make the retry tests pass
steps: Create a Goal Loop with a concrete goal, acceptance criteria, and budget.
Follow each iteration as the agent plans, executes, and evaluates its result.
Inspect the evidence and stop or redirect the loop when the work needs judgment.

chapters.title: Connect the steps
chapters.heading: A repeatable release check
steps: Open Workflows and build a graph from the steps your process needs.
Connect agent work, conditions, and approval nodes. Choose how the workflow starts.
Run it and inspect each node. Use the run view to investigate a failed step.

chapters.title: Put a report on a schedule
chapters.heading: Morning checkout health report
steps: Create a Scheduled Task with a prompt, provider, and schedule.
Choose the timezone and report destination. Check when it will run next.
Inspect the generated report and execution history before relying on the routine.

chapters.title: Meet your personal agent
chapters.heading: Atlas release assistant
steps: Open Personal Agents and create a named persona. Pin its provider and model.
Add schedules and useful memory. Chat with the agent whenever you need it.
Inspect its reports and shared rooms to follow the conversations between agents.

title: Follow the data
desc: Connect to a system, inspect a record, and test the contract around it.

chapters.title: Start with a connection
chapters.heading: Your systems, one starting point
steps: Open Connections to find saved terminals, databases, and Kafka clusters.
Choose a profile and connect. Use the configured SSH tunnel when the system requires one.
For SSH, open the terminal or SFTP browser to inspect files on the host.

chapters.title: Ask a precise question
chapters.heading: Find recent checkout failures
steps: Open a database from Connections. Select its database and inspect the schema.
Write a query, or use the assistant to draft one. Read it before running.
Inspect the results. Use the grid, JSON viewer, and export for a closer look.

chapters.title: Follow the event
chapters.heading: checkout.events
steps: Open a Kafka cluster from Connections. Select a topic and inspect its partitions.
Choose where to start reading and fetch a bounded set of messages.
Inspect a message key, headers, and payload to follow the event through the system.

chapters.title: Check the response
chapters.heading: Inspect the checkout endpoint
steps: Open API and choose or create a request. Set its method, URL, and environment.
Review headers, authentication, and body before sending the request.
Inspect the response, then save the request in a collection for next time.

title: Operate the cloud
desc: Move from an AWS account to a workload and the logs that explain it.

chapters.title: Choose the right account
chapters.heading: Atlas staging
steps: Open AWS and select the account you intend to inspect. Complete sign in if required.
Choose the region and service. Browse buckets, queues, instances, or databases.
Keep the account and region visible as you move between resources.

chapters.title: Read the resource signals
chapters.heading: Checkout database health
steps: Open an AWS resource and inspect its available metrics. Choose the time range.
Read the chart alongside the resource details to narrow the investigation.
Use the related service view when you need to inspect the underlying resource.

chapters.title: Find the workload
chapters.heading: checkout-api
steps: Open Kubernetes and select a saved cluster, or import an EKS cluster from AWS.
Choose a namespace you can access. Find the workload and open its details.
Use the Pods tab to inspect the pods belonging to that workload.

chapters.title: Read what happened
chapters.heading: Follow the checkout logs
steps: Open the workload Logs tab to inspect output from its pods.
Follow new lines and narrow the output to the event you are investigating.
Use pod details, events, or an exec session when the next step needs deeper inspection.

title: Improve the system
desc: Tune agent tools and skills, then understand the work they produce.

chapters.title: Choose the tools agents use
chapters.heading: A deliberate tool surface
steps: Open MCP Control Plane to inspect connected servers and their tools.
Review which capabilities an agent can access and how policies govern calls.
Use the audit view to investigate a governed tool invocation.

chapters.title: Make good practice reusable
chapters.heading: A focused review skill
steps: Open the skill library to inspect installed skills and their versions.
Read the instructions and usage scope before choosing a skill for a task.
Use focused skills to make your expectations explicit and reusable.

chapters.title: Evaluate before promoting
chapters.heading: Which skill works better?
steps: Open Skills Lab to browse, edit, evaluate, or review a skill.
Run a benchmark with a concrete task and inspect the validation results.
Compare runs and evidence before promoting the version you want to keep.

chapters.title: Understand cost and progress
chapters.heading: Read the shape of your work
steps: Open Usage and choose a period to inspect tokens and cost across providers.
Use the breakdowns to understand which models and sessions account for the usage.
Open Insights for a report, then inspect its evidence and suggested actions.

chapters.title: Extend your workspace
chapters.heading: Add the tools your team needs
steps: Open Plugins to inspect installed extensions and their configuration.
Choose a plugin to review its capabilities and current status.
Open its page from the sidebar when it provides a workspace tool.

title: Take Otto with you
desc: Keep the conversation and context close, across windows and devices.

chapters.title: Continue the conversation
chapters.heading: A conversation that stays connected
steps: Connect Slack or Telegram in Channels settings and configure the bridge.
Start from a thread and send the agent a clear request.
Follow the responses in the same conversation, or open the session in Otto.

chapters.title: Bring a session with you
chapters.heading: Your Mac does the work
steps: Enable remote access when you want to use Otto from a phone or tablet.
For a guest, create a scoped session link and choose viewer or editor access.
Set an expiry and revoke the link when it is no longer needed.

chapters.title: Give each task a window
chapters.heading: Two tasks, room for both
steps: Choose File, New Window to open another Otto window.
Keep a session in one window and the related review or data in another.
Arrange the windows for the task. Otto restores your windows on relaunch.

chapters.title: Show exactly what you mean
chapters.heading: Give the agent the visual context
steps: Press Command Control Shift Two and drag to capture a region.
Annotate the detail you want the agent to notice. The image is on your clipboard.
Paste it into the session and explain what needs to change.
